<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Relaying NES feedback from @aschackmull:

> There's one particular thing that's come up a lot. I'm pretty good at spotting typos myself, and Copilot is also pretty good at spotting typos, and this ends up clashing. Here's how: I make some edit that contains a typo, typically an identifier with a missing letter, or missing the closing brace or parenthesis of a method or expression. Copilot finds this and shows the missing character in a next-edit suggestion. Visually this is so subtle that when I then glance at the code, everything looks right to me - I fail to spot the typo, because the missing character is shown, so I don't accept the suggestion because I don't notice it, and then I proceed to wonder why it doesn't compile.
> 
> I guess the main problem is that tiny suggestions like inserting a missing letter or missing closing parenthesis is simply too visually subtle for me to notice, so I end up being confused about what is actually part of my file and what is merely a suggested addition.
> 
> Traditional highlighting using red squiggly underlines to highlight my error would likely have been a much better visual cue that something was missing, but it's possible that NES needs something completely different, so I'm not suggesting to use red squigglies exactly  - but it should be more visually noticeable.
> 
> And btw. for context re. my visual setup: I'm using neither light mode nor dark mode - I'm using grey mode, since that fits all external lighting conditions. My editor background colour is set to `"#d0d0c0"`

We've gotten feedback before that it can be easy to accidentally accept an NES - I wonder if there's anything specific for very minor code edits that we might want to consider here.

title: In-line suggestions stop working after a note in code...

labels.name: bug

body:
Type: Bug When editing a Markdown file, Copilot completely stops producing suggestions starting from the point where the phrase “tit-for-tat” appears. Suggestions continue to work normally before that phrase, but nothing is produced after it. Removing or renaming the phrase restores normal behavior. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Create or open a Markdown file. 2. Type content normally — Copilot suggestions appear as expected. 3. Add the phrase **“tit-for-tat”** anywhere in the document. 4. Continue writing _after_ that phrase. **Expected Behavior** Copilot should continue providing suggestions normally after that phrase. **Actual Behavior** Copilot provides **no suggestions** at all beyond that point in the file. **Hypothesis** This looks like an over-triggered safety or content-filter mechanism. The phrase itself is benign and commonly used in game theory / strategy / computer science contexts, so it seems to be incorrectly classified as unsafe. title: Copilot auto-complete is much too aggressive
body:
Type: Bug When you are just writing code, there is something that tries to give you auto-complete AI suggestions to "help" you with the code you're writing (I think it's GitHub Copilot). The problem is that these inline suggestions show up way too fast and move your code around visually, and tab seems to accept them, so if you're doing something easy and normal like adding an if statement and changing the tabbing of the code inside, or even just rearranging existing code, you can easily end up accepting the auto-complete suggestion by accident and then having to undo the suggestion and try to figure out how to make VS Code write only the code you were trying to write without any of the extra AI-suggested goo. While I think inline AI suggestions can be useful, they are currently much too aggressive and it's way too easy to accidentally end up accepting them instead of writing the code you were trying to write. They also interfere with the natural flow of writing code and force you to analyze the AI's suggestions to see if they're helpful or not. body:
Type: Bug editor.inlineSuggest.suppressSuggestions setting is not working. When enabled, the editor will still trash the (copilots) inline suggestion with the suggestion widget and I have to manually press Esc key to dismiss the suggestion widget to actually see the inline suggestion. The setting is described such that it should hide the suggest widget as long as the inline suggestion is available, but toggling it off vs on shows no difference in behavior. See the video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QWjsQnVVnMo As you can see, toggling the setting on or off has no effect. This makes trying to use Copilot inside VSCode very painful. The only way to make inline suggestion persist while typing is completely disabling suggest on type by: ``` "editor.quickSuggestions": { "other": "off", "comments": "off", "strings": "off" } ``` However if that is required, then there is no point of the editor.inlineSuggest.suppressSuggestions existing, because then it would have no purpose. It's current purpose seems to be ability for inline suggestions and suggestion list widget to coexist without having to disable the one or the other. title: Incorrect quote characters used for replacement in Python expression Copilot suggestion

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
Type: Bug # Description The code suggestion, while valid Python, is incorrect and highly unlikely to be what the user wants. title: 📌 Feedback: Make completions behavior less aggressive / more configurable

labels.name: under-discussion
labels.description: Issue is under discussion for relevance, priority, approach

labels.name: NES
labels.description: Issues related to the next edit suggestions feature

body:
We’ve heard ongoing feedback that GitHub Copilot’s completion suggestions can feel overly aggressive or intrusive at times. This issue aims to consolidate and track all related requests around customizing when and how completions are triggered. If you've landed here, you're likely looking for a way to make Copilot feel more tailored to your workflow. ## 📢 Configurable delay setting now available in VS Code Insiders Adding the following to [your settings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/settings#_settings-json-file) lets you control the delay (in milliseconds) before a suggestion appears after you start typing (e.g., I have set below 3 seconds): ```json "editor.inlineSuggest.minShowDelay": 3000, ``` Caveats: - This currently works only in VS Code Insiders + with latest pre-release version of the GitHub Copilot and GitHub Copilot Chat extensions - This will end up in delaying both [completions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/ai-powered-suggestions#_inline-suggestions) and [next edit suggestions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/ai-powered-suggestions#_next-edit-suggestions) - This feature is still under development, and we’ve noticed that the interaction between completions and NES behaves a bit differently with this setting. While we’re investigating, we'd value your feedback!
Other workarounds ## Other workarounds ### Option 1: Disable **_auto_**-suggestions (i.e., enable manually triggering suggestions) If you prefer to trigger completions on demand (i.e., only when you ask for them), you can disable automatic suggestions in your user settings: ```json "github.copilot.enable": { "*": false } ``` Then trigger completions manually using the default keybinding, `Alt + \`, or [customize your keybinding](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/keybindings#_keyboard-shortcuts-editor) for the `editor.action.inlineSuggest.trigger` command. More info can be found in the [VS Code docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/ai-powered-suggestions#_enable-or-disable-code-completions). ### Option 2: Snooze Copilot You can also temporarily disable all code completions in the editor via the Snooze functionality: Additional details can be found in the [comment below](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/13340#issuecomment-3028248201).
## We'd love your input! As an alternative, please react to this issue with emojis to indicate which options you’d like us to consider supporting beyond the current “on-demand” mode: - 🚀 Configurable delay before suggestions appear (e.g., number of milliseconds of pause after typing) - Available now in latest VS Code Insiders! - 👀 Single-line suggestion mode (limit completions to one line) - Other ideas -- please leave a comment to let us know! Your feedback helps us strike the right balance between helpfulness and interruption. Thanks for helping us improve Copilot!

title: NES/Inline Completion - Get more information on show

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Work not yet planned for a specific release.

body:
# Problem statement

Compared to the simplified context of ghostText, which would appear only after users cursor, providing guarantees around visibility, NES does not elicit the same behavior.

With possibility of suggestions being collapsed/out of view or presented in views which might not be properly readable/understandable it would be interesting for the engineering teams to understand in more detail what is happening in the guts of inlineCompletion flow.

e.g. which view is being presented, what is the visible range, what is the actual decoration that is shown (since there may be some arbitrary minification applied)

# Proposal

Add additional info property on the `handleDidShow()` function, which could send back to the provider:

```
viewName: string // e.g. sideBySide, lineReplacement
visibleRanges: Range[] // all the ranges that are visible to the user. Note that diff view can have multiple
edits: TextEdit[] // Diff used for visualisaiton, which can be minified compared to the original edit
cursor: Position // The current cursor position
```

For example in NES, this would mean that e.g. when user is shown a collapsed suggestion outside of screen, and scrolls to it, we could capture multiple events, allowing to distinguish between user intent to preview and arbitrary scroll. Once the view changes, e.g. to sideBySide it is a much stronger signal of visibility that a simple shown signal, which is now sent once the inlineEdit object is created inside the inlineCompletionsModel.

Happy to contribute with the change

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->

<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.81.1
- OS Version: Development done in MacOS Ventura (Version 13.5), occurs in all OSes.

## USE-CASE:
We are currently using Inline suggestions, and the text that goes in as the parameter is a snippetString. The snippet string is used as we need tab stops as the inline suggestion is committed.

## BUG:
We have noticed something unusual:
All the strings are passed through a function that converts them to snippet strings and adds tab stops to a particular substring if it matches a regex. 
For the cases where no tab stops are added, the indentation seems to be fine.
But, for the cases where tab stops are added, on committing the inline suggestion, extra indentation appears.

Eg of no indentation changes:
![ezgif-2-d435563887](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/42550351/87aab291-352c-47ab-ab3e-f6b11438358a)


Eg of change in indentation when tab-stops are added:
![ezgif-2-565c0ab68b](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/assets/42550351/e25b72ba-2581-4f65-aa8f-5d3027a97441)


## CODE:
Here's the code that does the conversion:
```typescript
export function convertToSnippetString(suggestion: string): string {
  const regex = /({{ )(_[a-zA-Z_]\w*_)( }})/gm;
  const matches = [...suggestion.matchAll(regex)];

  let modifiedSuggestion = suggestion;

  let counter = 0;
  matches.forEach((matchArray) => {
    const exactMatch = matchArray[2]; // get only the variable, without the braces
    counter = counter + 1;
    modifiedSuggestion = modifiedSuggestion.replace(
      exactMatch,
      `\$\{${counter}:${exactMatch}\}`
    ); // replace the match with tab stop syntax according to vscode snippet strings, i.e., ${1:foo}
  });

  let newIndentedSuggestion = modifiedSuggestion;

  return newIndentedSuggestion;
}
```

Here's how it is called:
```typescript
    // convert text to snippet string
    const insertTextSnippetString = new vscode.SnippetString(
      convertToSnippetString(insertText)
    );

    const inlineSuggestionItem = new vscode.InlineCompletionItem(
      insertTextSnippetString
    );
    inlineSuggestionUserActionItems.push(inlineSuggestionItem);
```

Let us know if this is a bug from the vscode code side or if there's some implementation error in the code.

title: Extensions can provide hover UI for inline completion

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

From https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/165988#issuecomment-1349679114 : 

# Problem

Currently (afaik) there is no way for mutliple inline-suggestions extensions to behave in a cooperative manner. So for example, plugins like GitHub Copilot shows a `Open GitHub Copilot` label in the inline-suggestions hover affordance, even with other plugins (such as [AWS Toolkit](https://github.com/aws/aws-toolkit-vscode)) are actively providing suggestions:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55561878/207440901-e2e5df04-b617-41f2-b237-0f488b37849e.png)

AWS Toolkit provides suggestions from [CodeWhisperer](https://aws.amazon.com/codewhisperer/). To do so, 

1. we implement [vscode.InlineCompletionItemProvider](https://github.com/aws/aws-toolkit-vscode/blob/c146b6e8edb92396d21746efdd03351c2c47475c/src/codewhisperer/service/inlineCompletionService.ts#L142).
2. we also [override "editor.action.inlinesuggest.shownext"](https://github.com/aws/aws-toolkit-vscode/blob/c146b6e8edb92396d21746efdd03351c2c47475c/src/codewhisperer/service/inlineCompletionService.ts#L179-L191)  and related commands _when CodeWhisperer is providing suggestions_ so that the inline suggestion popup `Next` and `Previous` buttons provide CodeWhisperer suggestions.

@alexdima @hediet is there a better way for vscode extensions to provide inline suggestions without conflicting with other inline suggestions extensions?

As a workaround, old versions of AWS Toolkit  _temporarily disabled_ the `editor.hover.enabled` setting. But that is a fragile workaround (which reduces functionality) and causes issues like https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/165988 .  

We've since removed that workaround. But now on mouse-hover, users that have installed GitHub Copilot will see a popup with a `Open GitHub Copilot` button (while CodeWhisperer is providing suggestions), which is very confusing.

# Expected behavior

Extensions that provide inline suggestions should be able to co-exist and not conflict with each other. If extension A is providing suggestions, it should be able to provide the inline-suggestions UI without conflict from other extensions.

Alternatively, similar to LSP, inline-suggestions could be "merged", and then multiple extensions would provide buttons on the inline-suggestions hover UI.

# Related

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/167042
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/146921

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Currently, when we display indented inline suggestion, the user needs to tab until the cursor is at the same location as the beginning of the text in the inline suggestion. 
This however is problematic if the suggestion is not exactly at the tab stop point (for example tab is set to 4 spaces in editor setting but displayed suggestion is on 6 spaces indentation) - it means users are often accidentally dismissing suggestion (by moving the cursor past suggestion). The workaround from a user point of view is that they need to use space to move the cursor precisely to the location of ghost text, however it's not super discoverable/obvious to users

I could potentially see 2 solutions here: 
* If the user press tab in a situation where it would move the cursor past suggestion, insert only as many spaces as required to put the cursor at the suggestion (from my earlier example - insert only 2 spaces, to put the cursor at 6 spaces), and next tab would accept suggestion normally.
* Or, if the tab would move the cursor past the suggestion, accept the suggestion. 

CC: @hediet

title: Inline proposals needs accessibility love

labels.name: accessibility
labels.description: Keyboard, mouse, ARIA, vision, screen readers (non-specific) issues

body:
Feedback from @isidorn:

Here are some suggestion on how to improve the accessibility of the inline propsals:

1. Once you are on an inline proposal pressing Ctrl + K, Ctrl + I, triggers the hover and moves focus into it -> very cool. However it would be nice if the `left` and `right` keybindings would move focus inside the hover on the actions. So that keyboard users can easily trigger the hover and use `left` and `right` to move the suggestion.
2. Bonus on top of that when Ctrl + K, Ctrl + I is triggered we should remember the previously focused element so it is focused again
3. Once an inline suggestion is shown we should probably use an aria alert to notify the user. Something like: `suggestion: CONTENT`. This is not the best experience but I think might be a good start. We do a similar things for parameter hints

Once we polish this a bit and there is a public way to try this out we should definitely share it with our a11y community to get better feedback.

Testing #264253

in a regular python file (part at the beginning)
1. make an edit 10 -> 5 (timestamp 0:03)
2. NES appears suggesting 5 -> 10 (timestamp 0:04)
3. I click to different lines (like at timestamp 0:11)
4. I still see the NES suggestion (it does get overruled by a new NES at timestamp 0:11 but I can still see the NES)

in a notebook

labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

labels.name: NES

body:
- [ ] :runner: Experiment to enable the Jupytext alternative Notebook format in NES
    - [x] Enable this
- [ ] Telemetry: Measure survival rate in Exp
  - Compare survival/telemetry for regular NES vs regular notebook cells vs unified notebook
- [ ] Golden Scenarios for cross cell NES https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/5701
- [ ] Notebook NES: Fails to show suggested change after suggesting to go to next cell (see here for details https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/264497)

**Add the following setting**
```
"github.copilot.chat.advanced.notebook.alternativeNESFormat.enabled": true, // Gives `Go To Next Edit`
"github.copilot.chat.notebook.enhancedNextEditSuggestions.enabled":true
```

## When/How to display/trigger NES in other cells
* [ ] Display `Go To Next Edit`: User in Cell 1 and there are suggested changes in Cell 2
* [ ] Should we display NES in cells after user edits a cell and runs it and then advances to the next cell
    * Users workflow is make changes to cell 1, run this
    * Should we wait till user sets focus to next cell in order to trigger NES for the next cell?
    * Can we instead proactively let user know that there are possible changes in next cell?
* [ ] Auto trigger NES completions when user sets focus to next cell after having modified another cell in same doc
    * Assume user changes cell 1
        * User sets focus or uses down arrow to go to next cell
        * We should trigger NES in this next cell
    * Assume user changes cell 1, next runs the cell
        * User keeps running the cell and tweaking cell 1, but never updates any other text document
        * After 30 minutes user goes to cell 10
        * We should trigger NES as user was still editing this notebook & didn't modify anything else in the interim

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Developers are used to tools which auto-format their code for them (Prettier, format on save, etc). When working with Next Edit Suggestions, the suggestion frequently is to simply format the recently modified code. This is distracting and slows down development, as it takes time to process what the suggestion is. It does not matter whether I accept or ignore the suggestion, as the code will be formatted automatically by other tools, and so it wastes time and slows down actual development.

I'd like to suggest a setting to disable formatting-only modifications from Next Edit Suggestions. Alternatively, we could use custom instructions specifically for Next Edit Suggestions to request no formatting-only modifications.

labels.name: verified

labels.description: Issues related to the next edit suggestions feature

body: I've been hearing increased interest (cc @hawkticehurst) in a keybinding to manually trigger NES or completions. I've pointed folks to the `Trigger Next Edit Suggestion` command, and @Tyriar had helpful feedback on it. He got both of the following (notification about no suggestions, and also an actual NES) at the same time (after ~1 second): He disabled inline completions, which could be the cause of the notification. But regardless, this notification shouldn't happen because the command is specifically about NES. It also seemed to respect delay/debounce he had set. I believe we don't largely guide users to this command, so some of these behaviors may be currently expected, but with increasing interest in this ability to trigger NES, I think addressing this could be quite helpful.

body:
- [ ] :runner: Experiment to enable the Jupytext alternative Notebook format in NES
    - [x] Enable this
- [ ] Telemetry: survival rate
  - Compare survival/telemetry for regular NES vs regular notebook cells vs unified notebook
- [x] Tests (scenarios for cross cell NES, etc),
- [x] Improve Trigger Events for cross cell NES
  - Better triggers for NES: alt format gives us a better "Cursor_move" event, what else?)
- [x] Explore enabling suggestions for other cells
  - we filter them out today, and they are cached
  - do we have other ways to suggest actions to other cells
    - Can we trigger nes command on other cells
    - What do we need to make this happen for other cells?
    - Can we implement short term solutions?
- [x] Improvements authoring stests for notebooks
  - Find whats missing and add it
- [x] Improve issue reporting for notebooks
  - Existing command works well
  - Added a new command to report with required data as well
- [ ] Golden Scenarios for cross cell NES https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/5701

**Add the following setting**
```
"github.copilot.chat.advanced.notebook.alternativeNESFormat.enabled": true,
"github.copilot.chat.notebook.enhancedNextEditSuggestions.enabled":true
```

## When/How to display/trigger NES in other cells
* [ ] Display `Go To Next Edit`: User in Cell 1 and there are suggested changes in Cell 2
* [ ] Should we display NES in cells after user edits a cell and runs it and then advances to the next cell
    * Users workflow is make changes to cell 1, run this
    * Should we wait till user sets focus to next cell in order to trigger NES for the next cell?
    * Can we instead proactively let user know that there are possible changes in next cell?
* [ ] Auto trigger NES completions when user sets focus to next cell after having modified another cell in same doc
    * Assume user changes cell 1
        * User sets focus or uses down arrow to go to next cell
        * We should trigger NES in this next cell
    * Assume user changes cell 1, next runs the cell
        * User keeps running the cell and tweaking cell 1, but never updates any other text document
        * After 30 minutes user goes to cell 10
        * We should trigger NES as user was still editing this notebook & didn't modify anything else in the interim

NES feature is a very good idea, it really helps to catch issues beforehand, but sometimes it gets in your way of coding, when i'm trying to indent the code (in places where we have to be vary careful, like YML or Python files) doing `tab` highlights first the github completion first instead doing an actual `tab` in the code.

Also it is becoming difficult to handle because before when the greyed code suggestions were in the way of indentation i could dismiss those with an `esc` and then do a normal `tab`, now NES gets highlighted and i do an `esc`, it closes the suggestion but the cursor is still selecting the suggestion collapsed and if i do a tab at that moment it applies the suggestion, even where i'm not coding. body:
We're currently using one accessible view content provider for both inline and next edit suggestions https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d9fd8a5eebc1385eaad269ddf5b8865fc6191e26/src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/inlineCompletionsAccessibleView.ts#L42. 

Because of this, they currently share the verbosity key, which allows users to disable the hint about the accessible view. 

We need to have a separate one so that next edit suggestion verbosity can be managed independently.  Since it's a new feature, users will benefit from the hint, while many users will have already disabled verbosity for inline suggestions.
